subject: Cost alignment: budget bands, token targets & residency impact
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@brightflow.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — token ranges, target $/1M, and regional residency note

Hi Sam — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + the asks I promised to surface.

Call summary (short):
- BrightFlow use case: customer-facing summarization + in-product copilots for analytics dashboards.
- Primary models: 8k and 16k context generator flows; occasional long-form batch jobs for monthly reports.
- Key constraint: some EU customers require data residency within EU; this will likely affect where we serve a portion of traffic.

Volumes & budget you quoted on the call:
- Low band: ~50M tokens / month
- Mid band: ~250M tokens / month
- High band: ~1.4B tokens / month (expected within 12–18 months at peak)
- You mentioned a blended target of roughly $300–$420 per 1M tokens as the acceptable unit cost range across that growth curve.

Preliminary unit economics (hosted estimates, US region):
- Redwood hosted (US): ~ $290 / 1M tokens (baseline, mixed model variants, default batching/caching)
- Redwood hosted (EU): ~ $335 / 1M tokens (roughly +15% region delta due to infra & local capacity premiums)
- Data residency add-on (when we keep data fully in-customer-region control + isolated VPC/private control plane): +~15% on top of region price (applies when EU-only residency is required)

Implications / notes:
- If you route EU customers to EU-only residency, expect incremental cost versus serving everything from US. We can do hybrid routing (US for public/global, EU for residency-requesting customers) to optimize blended cost.
- Model variant selection (quantized LLM vs fp16) and KV-cache sharing will materially change per-token cost — we can run a quick workload profile to tighten these numbers.

Deliverables I’ll send after this note:
- Formal estimate (attached draft PDF) with three pricing bands and blended projections
- CSV with regional cost line items per model variant (attached)

Can you confirm: (1) the expected split of EU-residency traffic today (rough %), and (2) whether the procurement team needs an estimated one-line item for forecasting or a full contract-level SOW?

If you prefer, we can schedule a short procurement / finance sync next week to walk the numbers.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW_estimate_Q2_v3.pdf (draft pricing bands)
Attachment: residency_cost_breakdown.csv (per-region line items)

From: Sam Torres <s.torres@brightflow.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@brightflow.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — token ranges, target $/1M, and regional residency note

Hey Kimberly — thanks for the recap and the fast turn. A few quick clarifications: 

- Volume split: right now ~30% of traffic is EU-residency required (mostly EU-based enterprise customers); we expect that to grow to ~45% over 12 months.
- Budgeting: finance gave me an internal target of ~$350 / 1M tokens as the stretch target for 2027. They said anything consistently above $420 / 1M will be hard to justify without offsetting offsets (e.g., committed terms, reserved capacity).
- Procurement asks: they want a one-page estimate for Q3 spend first, then a full SOW when numbers look good.

Action items on our side:
- I’ll confirm the EU-residency percent with Julia and send a short note by Friday.
- Procurement prefers a pricing line per region, and a note on any dedicated-reserved options that would lower unit price (commitment tiers).

Sam
VP Product, BrightFlow Analytics
s.torres@brightflow.ai

On Wed, Jul 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@brightflow.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — token ranges, target $/1M, and regional residency note — next steps

Hi Sam / Julia — following up after your note. I’ve attached the official draft estimate and a CSV breakdown of the regional/residency line items so procurement can drop the one-page number into forecasting. Summary of the updated items based on your feedback: 

Updated assumptions used in the attached estimate:
- Volume bands used: 50M /mo, 250M /mo, 1.4B /mo (same as call)
- Blended EU-residency split used for the draft: 30% EU-residency (per your note) — we can update when you confirm final split.
- Pricing rows included: Hosted US, Hosted EU, Data-residency add-on, Dedicated reserved (12-mo commit) discount row.

Key numbers from the draft (rounded):
- Hosted US baseline: $290 / 1M tokens
- Hosted EU baseline: $335 / 1M tokens
- Data-residency add-on: +15% (applies to the relevant EU traffic rows)
- Committed Dedicated estimate: as low as $230 / 1M tokens at top-tier volumes under a 12-mo reserved commit (requires model pinning and predictable burst profiles)

What I need from you to finalize:
1) Confirm the EU-residency % (we used 30% in the attached draft).
2) Confirm whether procurement wants the one-page estimate as a PDF or a single-line item in their internal forecast (we can do both).
3) If you want us to show a dedicated-reserved option, confirm whether BrightFlow is open to a 12-month commit and an expected monthly peak (just rough is fine).

Proposed next steps (short):
- You confirm the EU % and procurement format (by Fri Jul 17)
- I’ll send an updated PDF and a cleaned HubSpot deal line (linked in email)
- Optional: 30-min procurement call week of Jul 20 to lock terms and discuss SOW cadence

If helpful, Rishi (cc’d) can run a quick model-variant sensitivity & caching impact analysis to show how unit price moves with a 10–30% increase in cache hit rate. Lauren can provide the dedicated capacity schedule and how that maps to commit tiers.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the EU split.

— Kimberly
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129
